body: V1.7 should establish the foundation for long-lived, domain-adaptable AWG vaults. The core path is: agent-authored vault operating templates, structured content fields and blocks, presentation primitives rendered by the viewer, and lifecycle/freshness conventions that make current vs historical knowledge explicit. The goal is not to ship many domain-specific templates, nor to rebuild Obsidian or allow arbitrary HTML. The goal is to make each vault self-describing and easy for agents to maintain while giving humans a glanceable generated surface.

body: AWG should ship template mechanics, generic guidance, and minimal examples. The actual domain template should live inside the vault as durable AWG knowledge: purpose, node taxonomy, edge conventions, view strategy, review policy, agent rules, and presentation expectations. This supports specialized domains without making the core project responsible for guessing every industry. Template changes should be explicit, reasoned, and reviewable so every agent pass does not reshape the vault.

body: A vault-local template should support draft, active, needs_review, and superseded states. Agents may propose improvements, but active convention changes need rationale, affected types/edges/views, migration notes, and ideally human review markers. Future agents should read the active template before creating knowledge and should record friction as questions/risks/tasks instead of repeatedly mutating the template.
summary: Vault templates need lifecycle, rationale, and review controls so future agents follow conventions without silently rewriting them every run.

body: AWG should avoid Markdown-only canonicals. Summary remains the retrieval and scan surface. Body is optional narrative detail for nuance. Fields are typed operational data agents can filter, validate, and maintain. Blocks are typed display primitives for the human viewer. Important operational truth should not only live in body text. This keeps AWG graph-first while still allowing richer explanation where it helps.
summary: Nodes need clear layers: concise summary for retrieval, optional body for nuance, structured fields for operations, and blocks for human presentation.
title: V1.7 requirement: structured node content

body: V1.7 should introduce a small block set: brief, callout, metric-row, table, checklist, task-queue, risk-list, decision-list, evidence-list, timeline, run-summary, bar-chart, line-chart, relationship-map, and status-board if feasible. Blocks should be data, not raw HTML or agent-authored CSS. The viewer owns styling and rendering. Agents choose the block that matches the information shape so humans get quick insight without reading a wall of text.

body: V1.7 should make the freshness contract more explicit. A node can be historical, current, proposed, superseded, stale, or needs_review; review_after and evidence should be used consistently. goal: Turn AWG V1.7 planning into implementation-grade spec

body: This node is the implementation-grade parent spec for AWG V1.7. V1.7 should make AWG more useful as a domain-agnostic shared agent brain without drifting into Markdown file sprawl, arbitrary HTML, hosted sync, daemons, vector search, or domain-specific template bundles. The implementation must preserve the append-only canonical log, deterministic compiler, project-local vaults, backward compatibility with older logs, unknown-field preservation, and stable agent-facing JSON. Definition of done: an agent can discover the active vault operating template, create/update richer nodes with concise summaries plus structured data, surface human-readable blocks in the viewer, identify stale/current/historical knowledge, receive conservative doctor suggestions, and follow an updated final loop that keeps AWG current while work is performed.
summary: Binding V1.7 implementation spec for vault-local operating templates, structured node content, typed presentation blocks, freshness/currentness, viewer surfacing, diagnostics, and tests.
title: AWG V1.7 implementation-grade spec

body: Implementation contract: summary remains required and concise for retrieval, list views, handoff, and search snippets. body is optional narrative context for nuance and may use safe markdown-lite rendering later, but operational truth must not live only in body. fields is an optional JSON object for domain and template-defined machine-readable data; it must preserve unknown keys and reject only non-JSON values. blocks is an optional ordered array of validated display data for the human viewer. freshness/currentness metadata should use explicit fields such as currentness, review_after, verified_at, source_of_truth, stale_reason, supersedes, and superseded_by where compatible with existing conventions. evidence_required remains supported and should be honored by diagnostics/preflight. Older nodes without body, fields, blocks, or freshness metadata must compile unchanged.
summary: Nodes must separate retrieval summary, optional narrative body, structured fields, typed presentation blocks, freshness metadata, and evidence requirements.
title: V1.7 spec: structured node content model

body: Required command behavior: awg add node and awg update node should support body updates, repeated field assignment, JSON field import, block JSON append/replace, evidence-required, review-after, anchors, tags, importance, confidence, type, title, summary, and status. Field and block options must be explicit and deterministic; malformed JSON should produce clear errors and should not append partial events. Existing --run, --no-run, and active-run attribution must apply to these writes. In JSON mode, return the normalized updated node fields and event ids. Do not require agents to manually edit .awg/log JSONL for normal rich node updates. Preserve unknown fields already present on nodes when updating a subset of fields.
summary: CLI writes should let agents add and update body, fields, blocks, freshness metadata, review cadence, anchors, and evidence requirements without manual JSONL edits.
title: V1.7 spec: node write and update contract

body: Every block must be JSON data, not HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, or arbitrary markdown. Common shape: {type, title?, summary?, tone?, data, sourceNodeIds?, targetNodeIds?}. type is a known primitive. title and summary are plain text. tone is a constrained enum such as info, success, warning, danger, neutral. data is primitive-specific JSON. sourceNodeIds and targetNodeIds are optional links used for traceability. The compiler should preserve valid blocks, warn on invalid blocks with node ids and block indexes, and avoid crashing the viewer. The viewer should render known blocks with shared design tokens and show a compact unsupported-block fallback for unknown future block types. Blocks must be deterministic, local-only, safe to render in static HTML, and small enough for lenses/handoff to budget.
summary: Blocks are safe JSON presentation primitives rendered by AWG; agents choose data shapes, while the viewer owns styling and sanitization.
title: V1.7 spec: typed presentation block contract

body: Answer to the first block schema scope question: prove the model with a small, composable primitive set instead of turning AWG into a UI framework. MVP primitives are brief for short structured narrative, callout for warnings or important state, metric-row for compact scalar values, table for structured records, checklist for acceptance or SOP items, node-list for typed references such as tasks risks decisions evidence, and timeline for ordered events. Defer line-chart, bar-chart, relationship-map, status-board, image, and custom domain primitives until the JSON block contract, compiler diagnostics, and viewer fallbacks are stable. This keeps V1.7 useful for code, SEO, content, business, and trading vaults without making presentation arbitrary.
summary: The first V1.7 block set should be small: brief, callout, metric-row, table, checklist, node-list, and timeline; charts/maps/status boards are deferred unless trivial.
title: V1.7 decision: first block primitive scope

body: Acceptance criteria: brief renders labeled key points or short paragraphs without crowding. callout renders tone, title, and text consistently. metric-row renders stable label/value/unit/status/trend items without layout shift. table renders columns and rows from JSON with truncation or wrapping for long values. checklist renders item status as pending, in_progress, done, skipped, or blocked and may link items to nodes. node-list renders referenced nodes by title/type/status/summary when available and degrades to ids when missing. timeline renders dated or ordered entries. All primitives must render in the static viewer without external dependencies, survive build/read/write cycles, appear in --json outputs, and fail safely when block data is malformed.
summary: Each MVP block primitive needs schema validation, static viewer rendering, JSON output preservation, fallback handling, and tests.
title: V1.7 spec: block primitive acceptance criteria

body: A vault-local operating template should be represented in the graph, not as a hidden side database and not as a bundle of core-maintained domain presets. Use regular nodes and edges with stable conventions. The active template should include: vault purpose, intended domain and audience, preferred node types and local subtypes, required fields by node type, required edge patterns, evidence rules, freshness/review cadence, presentation block preferences, agent start/during/finish rules, naming conventions, and examples. The template may be a cluster rooted at one active standard or policy node tagged template:operating. Related template sections should link with part_of, requires, recommends, or applies_to. Future agents must read the active template before creating domain knowledge.
summary: A vault operating template is durable AWG knowledge that defines purpose, taxonomy, edge conventions, fields, blocks, freshness rules, and agent rules for that vault.
title: V1.7 spec: vault-local operating template model

body: Answer to the template CLI scope question: do not build a full template authoring system or ship many domain starter packs in V1.7. Required foundation is the graph convention plus docs and generated agent instructions. A small read-only awg template status --json command is useful if low-risk: it should report active operating-template roots, template sections, missing recommended sections, needs_review template nodes, and the commands agents can use to inspect them. Creating or changing templates should remain normal awg add/update node and edge writes so the append-only model stays simple. Defer template init, template apply, template marketplace, and bundled industry-specific templates.
summary: V1.7 should add a read-only template status surface if small, while template creation and refinement remain normal AWG node and edge writes.
title: V1.7 decision: minimal template CLI scope

body: Acceptance criteria: an active operating template is discoverable through handoff, task lens, resume lens, and template status if implemented. Template nodes can be draft, active, needs_review, superseded, or archived. Any agent that changes active template guidance should record rationale, affected node types, affected edge conventions, affected fields/blocks, migration notes, and whether human review is needed. Normal agents should record friction as questions, risks, or tasks rather than silently rewriting the template. Doctor should warn about multiple active operating-template roots, template nodes stuck in needs_review, and missing high-value template sections such as purpose, taxonomy, freshness rules, and agent rules.
summary: Template changes must be explicit, attributable, reviewable, and resistant to agent churn.
title: V1.7 spec: template governance acceptance criteria

body: Implementation contract: use existing statuses where possible and add structured freshness fields rather than inventing a parallel lifecycle. current active knowledge should have enough evidence or provenance to trust. proposed knowledge should not be treated as operational truth. historical or superseded knowledge must remain available but clearly marked so future agents do not apply it as current. review_after should drive stale warnings. verified_at and evidence links should explain why a node is current. stale_reason should explain why a node needs review. supersedes and superseded_by may be node ids or represented by edges. Agents that change a feature, SOP, customer fact, trading assumption, content rule, SEO process, or business record must update or flag related current nodes in the same run.
summary: AWG should make current, historical, proposed, stale, superseded, and needs-review knowledge explicit and agent-maintainable.
title: V1.7 spec: freshness and currentness contract

body: Required agent loop: start with awg handoff, awg lens resume, and awg lens task for the goal. Before creating knowledge, run awg search and inspect related nodes. During work, update existing nodes when facts change, add evidence to completed work, record risks/questions/decisions, and add run notes for meaningful progress or blockers. Before finish, run awg build and awg doctor --fix-suggestions --json, address fatal errors and relevant warnings, mark stale affected nodes as needs_review or update them, then finish with awg run finish --status completed|partial|blocked|failed --summary ... --auto-handoff. If the agent intentionally leaves open planning risks or questions, it should document why in a run note or response so preflight warnings are explainable.
summary: Agents should search, update, evidence, and review AWG knowledge as part of normal work, not as an optional cleanup step.
title: V1.7 spec: automatic agent maintenance loop

body: Diagnostics should remain deterministic and conservative. Suggested checks: stale current nodes where review_after is past; evidence_required nodes without evidence; active requirements/processes/templates with low confidence; completed tasks lacking evidence; proposed decisions linked to completed implementation; multiple active operating templates; missing active operating template sections; orphaned nodes from recent runs; active risks/blockers touched in recent runs without review; invalid or unsupported blocks; malformed fields; and nodes marked current with no verification signal when the active template requires one. doctor --fix-suggestions --json should return code, nodeIds, message, severity, suggestedCommands, and optional rationale. Suggestions should never delete data or rewrite history.
summary: Doctor should provide conservative structured suggestions for stale, conflicting, missing-evidence, orphaned, and template-health issues without mutating state.
title: V1.7 spec: freshness diagnostics and fix suggestions

body: Viewer contract: preserve the existing clean overview and graph traversal architecture. Add block rendering where it improves comprehension: node detail, current view, handoff/run surfaces, and template status if implemented. Do not redesign the whole UI. Known blocks should render with existing design tokens, responsive constraints, stable spacing, and safe text handling. Raw body text may be shown as secondary detail, not the primary presentation for operational nodes with blocks. Overview should prefer curated summaries, active run, active template, unresolved risks/questions, stale/currentness pressure, and high-signal changed nodes. Node detail should show summary, fields, blocks, evidence, freshness, backlinks, run attribution, and diagnostics in a scannable order. Unknown or invalid blocks must not crash the viewer.
summary: The viewer should turn graph knowledge and typed blocks into glanceable surfaces without becoming a generic Markdown or HTML renderer.
title: V1.7 spec: human viewer presentation contract

body: Handoff should remain compact and budget-aware. Include current or most recent run, active operating template summary, important unresolved preflight or doctor items, nodes created/updated/evidenced by recent runs, stale current nodes affecting the goal, and recommended next actions. Handoff should include block-derived summaries only when they are concise; it should not dump full bodies or all blocks. lens task should use deterministic matching across title, summary, tags, body snippets, fields, block text values, related run goals, run notes, and touched nodes. It should include related template rules and freshness obligations when relevant to the goal. JSON output should expose enough structure for agents to select next actions without parsing prose.
summary: Handoff and task lens should surface active template guidance, relevant structured fields, block summaries, freshness warnings, and related run context within budget.
title: V1.7 spec: run-aware handoff and task lens contract

body: CLI contract: keep existing commands compatible. Extend add/update node with rich content options rather than adding a second authoring path. Add read-only template status if low-risk. Build/validate/doctor/handoff/lens/run status JSON should include fields, blocks, freshness metadata, template context, and relevant diagnostics without breaking older consumers. JSON keys should be stable, deterministic, and documented. In text mode, output should be compact and actionable. Errors should name the bad flag, node id, field path, or block index. No command should write outside the intended project .awg or managed global registry paths. No network, server, daemon, AI dependency, vector search, or arbitrary plugin execution.
summary: New V1.7 capabilities should be available through stable CLI commands and parseable JSON without requiring the viewer or manual log edits.
title: V1.7 spec: CLI and JSON contract

body: Compiler contract: parse older logs unchanged. Preserve unknown event and node fields unless intentionally normalized. Materialize node body, fields, blocks, freshness metadata, evidence_required, anchors, run attribution, and existing evidence arrays. Add derived indexes only when useful and deterministic: active template roots and sections, nodes by freshness/currentness, nodes with stale review_after, nodes with blocks, invalid block diagnostics, evidence-required gaps, and run-touched stale nodes. Build output should continue to write graph, nodes, edges, indexes, diagnostics, resume lens, current view, and static site. Invalid block or field structures should produce diagnostics and safe fallback data, not silent data loss. Strict mode may elevate severe validation issues if that matches existing behavior.
summary: The compiler should preserve rich node content, derive template/freshness/block indexes, and emit diagnostics without breaking older vaults.
title: V1.7 spec: compiler and materialization contract

body: Compatibility constraints: existing commands continue to work. Existing vaults without fields, blocks, templates, freshness metadata, or run attribution compile. Unknown fields are preserved. Generated artifacts are not source. Tests must isolate HOME and filesystem writes. The canonical model remains append-only JSONL. Non-goals: no MCP, daemon, hosted sync, plugin marketplace, Obsidian import, GitHub/Linear/Todoist sync, semantic/vector search, multi-user collaboration, arbitrary plugin execution, arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS, large UI redesign, or domain-specific template library in core. V1.7 may create generic mechanics and examples, but the actual domain operating template belongs inside each vault.
summary: V1.7 must stay local-first, deterministic, append-only, domain-agnostic, and backward compatible; major sync, AI, and plugin systems remain out of scope.
title: V1.7 spec: compatibility constraints and non-goals

The goal is to make each vault self-describing and easy for agents to maintain while giving humans a glanceable generated surface.

body: Template roots must declare fields.scope with one of vault, project, domain, task, agent, or custom, plus optional fields.appliesTo such as project ids, domain tags, path prefixes, anchors, or goal keywords. Multiple active templates are allowed only when scopes differ or applyTo selectors do not conflict. Selection precedence for a goal is: explicit template id, task/goal match, anchor/path match, project match, domain match, vault default. Diagnostics should warn on conflicting active templates at the same scope and selector, missing vault default, or selected template sections in needs_review. Materialized OperatingTemplateIndex should include activeRoots, selectedDefaultRootId, rootsByScope, sectionsByRootId, missingSections, conflicts, and diagnostics. Suggested compiled output is .awg/compiled/indexes/operating-templates.json plus inclusion in graph/index JSON if compatible.

body: This supersedes the earlier optional wording. V1.7 requires awg template status and awg template status --json. It is read-only and must not create, apply, or mutate templates. Text output should show selected active template roots, scope, missing recommended sections, conflicts, and next inspection commands. JSON shape: {ok, activeTemplateId, activeTemplates, rootsByScope, selectedForGoal?, missingSections, conflicts, warnings, suggestedCommands}. Optional --goal may select the template that would apply to a task goal. Template creation and refinement remain normal AWG add/update node and edge writes. Defer template init, template apply, bundled domain packs, marketplace behavior, and migrations.
summary: V1.7 should include awg template status as a read-only deterministic discovery surface for active operating templates.
title: V1.7 decision: require template status command

body: Canonical node field is freshness, preserving the existing shape. Schema: freshness.state is current, historical, proposed, stale, superseded, unknown, or not_applicable. freshness.last_verified, freshness.review_after, and freshness.superseded_at are ISO dates or datetimes. freshness.verified_by, freshness.source_of_truth, freshness.stale_reason, freshness.supersedes, and freshness.superseded_by are optional strings or node id arrays where appropriate. Compatibility: top-level review_after remains accepted and should normalize into freshness.review_after in materialized outputs. Existing freshness.last_verified remains accepted. Precedence: status rejected, archived, or superseded means not current even if freshness.state is current; status proposed means freshness.state cannot make it operational truth; status active/completed/resolved can be current only when freshness.state is current or absent. Doctor should warn on contradictory status/freshness pairs.
summary: Use nested freshness metadata as the canonical model and define exact state values, dates, compatibility, and precedence with status.
title: V1.7 spec: canonical freshness schema

body: Anchors are the bridge between work artifacts and graph knowledge. Supported anchor kinds remain file, symbol, url, command, doc, external, and may add domain-specific labels through fields without changing core kinds. Anchor values should be normalized enough for matching: file paths relative to vault root when possible, URLs without tracking parameters, symbols as path#name or language-native identifier, external as provider:key. lens task, search, handoff, and doctor should match goal text against title, summary, tags, anchors, body snippets, fields, and block text. Agents changing a file, route, URL, customer/site id, feature name, SOP, or external object should search anchors and related nodes before finishing. Doctor can warn when recently touched files or anchors have stale related nodes if that data is available locally.
summary: Agents need deterministic ways to find knowledge affected by code, URLs, customers, domains, files, features, and external objects.
title: V1.7 spec: impact and anchor discovery contract

body: Template sections may declare fieldRules as JSON data: {nodeType, field, required?, recommended?, default?, severity, description, example, allowedValues?, valueType?}. V1.7 should support warning-level validation for missing required or recommended fields in nodes covered by the active template. Fatal validation is deferred unless the project already opts into strict mode. Rules must be domain-agnostic and template-local. Examples: a customer record template may require fields.customerId and fields.owner; a research finding may recommend fields.claimType and fields.lastChecked; a code feature spec may require anchors for relevant files. doctor --fix-suggestions --json should suggest awg update node commands that add placeholders or mark nodes needs_review, not invent facts.
summary: Operating templates should define required and recommended fields by node type so guidance becomes actionable diagnostics, not only prose.
title: V1.7 spec: template-defined field rules

body: Granularity rule: a node should represent one durable thing agents may retrieve, update, evidence, or link. Use a short summary for scan and retrieval. Use body for nuance, rationale, examples, and acceptance criteria. Use fields for operational data that agents must filter or maintain. Use blocks for human-facing presentation. Split a node when parts have different lifecycle, owner, evidence, review cadence, or relationships. Keep together when splitting would force agents to read several nodes to understand one atomic fact or SOP. Spec and SOP nodes should usually be deeper than one sentence. Evidence nodes can stay small. Customer/business records should use fields and anchors for stable ids. Research findings should separate claim, evidence, status, and last verification. Decisions should include options, rationale, consequences, and links.
summary: Nodes should be precise retrieval units with enough depth for operation; summaries stay small, but spec/SOP/customer/research nodes may have substantial bodies, fields, and blocks.
title: V1.7 spec: node granularity standard

body: Canonical block shape: {schemaVersion:1,type,title?,summary?,tone?,data,sourceNodeIds?,targetNodeIds?}. Required common fields are schemaVersion, type, and data. MVP data shapes: brief {items:[{label?,text}]}; callout {text,actions?}; metric-row {items:[{label,value,unit?,status?,trend?}]}; table {columns:[{key,label,type?}],rows:[object]}; checklist {items:[{label,status,targetId?}]}; node-list {nodeIds:[id],reason?}; timeline {items:[{at?,label,summary?,nodeId?}]}. tone enum: neutral, info, success, warning, danger. checklist status enum: pending, in_progress, done, skipped, blocked. Limits should warn, not crash: max 25 blocks per node, max 100 KB total serialized blocks per node, max JSON depth 8, max table rows rendered by default 100, max cell preview 240 chars, no base64 blobs, no script/style/html execution.
summary: MVP block primitives need schemaVersion, primitive-specific required keys, examples, and warning-level size/depth guardrails.
title: V1.7 spec: block schemas, examples, and limits

body: The human surface needs a current effort view, reusing the existing current/run/viewer architecture instead of a redesign. It should be driven by active run plus graph state: run goal, agent, status, summary or latest notes, active template selected for the goal, nodes created/updated/touched, decisions made or still proposed, active risks/blockers touched, stale or needs-review touched nodes, evidence added, preflight warnings, handoff quality, and recommended next actions. The surface should be glanceable before drilling into graph traversal or node detail. It must avoid dumping full Markdown bodies. Use typed blocks when available, compact lists otherwise, and keep budget-like limits so a long run does not produce an unusable page.
summary: The viewer should show what the active agent run is trying to do, what changed, what is unresolved, and what happens next.
title: V1.7 spec: current effort human surface

body: Agents must not store raw API keys, passwords, private keys, seed phrases, payment card data, or secret tokens in AWG nodes, fields, blocks, bodies, evidence, or run notes. Use references to external secret managers or environment variable names instead. Nodes or fields may declare sensitivity as public, internal, confidential, secret_reference, or restricted. Viewer, handoff, and lens JSON should preserve data but text summaries should avoid overexposing restricted values when possible. Doctor should warn on obvious secret-like values in body, fields, blocks, and evidence command text using conservative patterns. Suggestions should replace raw secret value with a reference, never delete history automatically. This is domain-agnostic and applies to customer info, financials, trading systems, and business operations.
summary: AWG may hold business context, but should not become a raw secret store; sensitive fields need explicit markings and conservative diagnostics.
title: V1.7 spec: sensitive data and secret handling

body: Retrieval text extraction should remain deterministic and cheap. Index title, id, slug, type, status, summary, tags, anchors, selected body text, selected field keys and scalar values, block title/summary/text labels, linked node ids, run goal, and run notes. Suggested scoring priority: id/title/summary/tags highest; anchors and node type/status next; field keys and scalar values next; block title/summary/text next; body snippets lower and capped; run notes only for related-run selection. Cap indexed body at 4000 chars per node, fields at depth 4 and 200 scalar values, blocks at rendered text 4000 chars per node. Do not index huge arrays, binary-looking values, base64 payloads, or restricted secret-like values. JSON lens output should expose match categories so agents know why a node was included.
summary: Search, task lens, and handoff should extract deterministic text from body, fields, blocks, anchors, and run context with bounded scoring.

The compiler should preserve valid blocks, warn on invalid blocks with node ids and block indexes, and avoid crashing the viewer. The viewer should render known blocks with shared design tokens and show a compact unsupported-block fallback for unknown future block types. Blocks must be deterministic, local-only, safe to render in static HTML, and small enough for lenses/handoff to budget.

body:
Problem:
AWG has project-local vaults and a global registry, but real work often spans multiple repos or nested operating scopes. The client portal, Astro template, and Sanity schema are separate projects with separate AWG vaults, yet agents need to understand that changes in one can require coordinated updates in the others. Business brains may also have top-level operating knowledge with client-specific child vaults underneath.

Goal:
Introduce a local-first project topology layer that lets AWG describe relationships between vaults and expose cross-vault context to CLI, agent instructions, handoff, task lens, and viewer surfaces. The model should support parent/child, sibling, dependency, shared-source, deployment, owns, consumes, and related-project relationships without forcing one global merged graph.

Example shapes:
1. rd-client-portal depends on sanity-master-template for schema/content contracts and astro-master-template for rendered site behavior.
2. astro-master-template consumes Sanity data and may be deployed/controlled through client portal workflows.
3. Reavis Digital may have a business-level AWG vault for SOPs, pricing, services, ads, SEO, contacts, and operating rules, while client-specific AWG vaults can inherit or reference that business context without polluting the core business brain.

Requirements to explore:
- Registry entries need relationship metadata, not only switcher data.
- Nodes need optional project/vault anchors for cross-project relevance.
- Task lens and handoff should surface related vaults and the minimum necessary cross-vault context.
- Viewer should show a top-level project topology and allow drilling into related vaults.
- Agents need clear rules for when to update local knowledge, when to update a related vault, and when to leave a cross-project handoff.
- The design must stay local-first, deterministic, append-only where possible, and avoid daemon/server/sync creep.

Open design question:
The main unresolved choice is whether relationship metadata belongs primarily in ~/.awg/registry.json, in per-vault AWG nodes, or as a compiled overlay derived from both. The likely answer is a small registry topology plus per-vault durable nodes for richer semantics.

Decision:
V1.8 should introduce explicit cross-project topology. The global registry should remain a local control plane, but it should be able to store stable vault ids and lightweight relationships between registered vaults. Each vault remains canonical for its own durable knowledge. The compiler can derive a read-mostly federation overlay for task lens, handoff, doctor, and viewer surfaces.

Why this is the best foundation:
- It preserves project-local ownership and append-only vault history.
- It lets related projects be discovered without dumping every graph into context.
- It works for sibling repos, parent/child business-client structures, and dependency chains.
- It gives agents enough map context to know where related knowledge lives while keeping writes explicit.
- It avoids daemon, sync, database, server, and multi-user complexity.

Rejected alternatives:
1. One global merged graph: simpler to query, but ownership becomes unclear, context grows fast, and privacy/scope boundaries become fragile.
2. Folder hierarchy inference only: convenient, but too ambiguous; folder layout is not a reliable semantic relationship.
3. Automatic cross-vault writes: powerful but dangerous; agents could silently mutate the wrong business/client/project brain.
4. External sync or hosted coordination: too heavy for the local-first product and outside the current scope.

Final direction:
Start with explicit links, read-only traversal, deterministic indexes, and agent-facing prompts that require deliberate local-vault updates or cross-vault handoff notes when a related vault should be changed.

body:
Purpose:
The cross-vault contract should let AWG represent project families without collapsing them into one storage system. It must support multi-repo products, parent business brains with child client brains, and research/program brains with related execution projects.

Minimum contract:
- Each registered vault has a stable vault id, display name, path, scope, optional domain tags, and last_seen/build metadata.
- Registry topology stores lightweight relationships between vault ids. Relationship records should include fromVaultId, rel, toVaultId, optional summary, optional confidence, created_at, and updated_at.
- Relationship vocabulary should start small: parent_of, child_of, sibling_of, depends_on, provides_contract_for, consumes_contract_from, deploys_to, owns, related_to.
- Per-vault nodes can carry anchors or fields that reference a related vault and optional related node id.
- Compiled topology should resolve registered paths, missing vaults, relationship direction, cycles, stale builds, and related-vault summaries.
- Lenses should expose related-vault context only when relevant to the current goal, touched nodes, anchors, or topology edges.

Agent contract:
- Read related-vault summaries automatically when topology says they may matter.
- Before adding cross-project knowledge, decide whether it belongs in the current vault, a related vault, or a cross-vault handoff.
- Never silently mutate a related vault without an explicit command context and run attribution.
- If a change likely affects a related vault but the agent does not update it, record a cross-vault handoff item.

Human surface contract:
- Viewer overview may show current vault plus directly related vaults.
- A dedicated topology view should show project families and relationship health.
- Node detail should show cross-vault refs and affected related vaults without dumping the other vault contents.

Scale rule:

body:
Risks and mitigations:

1. Scope confusion
Agents may write client-specific facts into the business vault or global/product facts into a client vault. Mitigate with explicit vault ownership, visible target-vault prompts, run attribution, and handoff warnings when a related vault is affected but not updated.

2. Context explosion
A related-vault graph can become huge. Mitigate with direct-neighbor default traversal, hard budgets, summaries first, opt-in depth, and goal-matched retrieval only.

3. Stale cross-vault links
Related vaults may move, be deleted, or have stale compiled output. Mitigate with stable vault ids, path repair suggestions, last_seen/build metadata, and doctor warnings for missing/stale vaults.

4. Folder hierarchy false positives
Nested directories do not always mean parent-child knowledge ownership. Mitigate by treating folder layout as discovery evidence only; semantic relationships must be explicit.

5. Accidental cross-vault mutation
A command intended for the current project could modify a related vault. Mitigate by making cross-vault writes require explicit target-vault flags, confirmation in human CLI output, and run attribution in the target vault.

6. Security and privacy leakage
A high-level business vault could surface client-sensitive data, or a client vault could expose unrelated business data. Mitigate with no automatic global merging, summary-only default surfaces, sensitive diagnostics, and optional relationship visibility fields.

7. Cycles and ambiguous ownership
Project families can have cycles like portal <-> Astro <-> Sanity. Mitigate with relationship types, directionality, cycle diagnostics as warnings not fatal errors, and ownership-specific rels such as owns/provides_contract_for/consumes_contract_from.

8. Registry corruption or portability issues
The registry is a control plane and can drift from reality. Mitigate with schema validation, backups via append-like update events where practical, repair suggestions, and keeping canonical project knowledge inside project vaults.

9. Agents ignoring topology
The feature fails if agents do not check it. Mitigate by adding topology checks to handoff, lens task, generated AGENTS.md, and finish preflight when related-vault impacts exist.

10. Over-modeling too early
A large ontology could make AWG harder to use. Mitigate with a tiny relationship vocabulary, extension fields, and measured evolution from real dogfood cases.

Problem:
AWG has project-local vaults and a global registry, but real work often spans multiple repos or nested operating scopes. The client portal, Astro template, and Sanity schema are separate projects with separate AWG vaults, yet agents need to understand that changes in one can require coordinated updates in the others. Business brains may also have top-level operating knowledge with client-specific child vaults underneath.

Goal:
Introduce a local-first project topology layer that lets AWG describe relationships between vaults and expose cross-vault context to CLI, agent instructions, handoff, task lens, and viewer surfaces. The model should support parent/child, sibling, dependency, shared-source, deployment, owns, consumes, and related-project relationships without forcing one global merged graph.

Example shapes:
1. rd-client-portal depends on sanity-master-template for schema/content contracts and astro-master-template for rendered site behavior.
2. astro-master-template consumes Sanity data and may be deployed/controlled through client portal workflows.
3. Reavis Digital may have a business-level AWG vault for SOPs, pricing, services, ads, SEO, contacts, and operating rules, while client-specific AWG vaults can inherit or reference that business context without polluting the core business brain.

Requirements to explore:
- Registry entries need relationship metadata, not only switcher data.
- Nodes need optional project/vault anchors for cross-project relevance.
- Task lens and handoff should surface related vaults and the minimum necessary cross-vault context.
- Viewer should show a top-level project topology and allow drilling into related vaults.
- Agents need clear rules for when to update local knowledge, when to update a related vault, and when to leave a cross-project handoff.
- The design must stay local-first, deterministic, append-only where possible, and avoid daemon/server/sync creep.

Open design question:
The main unresolved choice is whether relationship metadata belongs primarily in ~/.awg/registry.json, in per-vault AWG nodes, or as a compiled overlay derived from both. The likely answer is a small registry topology plus per-vault durable nodes for richer semantics.

# V1.8 Implementation Contract: Identity, Topology, and Cross-Vault References

This is the implementation-grade contract for AWG V1.8 cross-project topology. It closes the gaps found by subagent review and should be treated as the source of truth for implementers.

## Scope Boundary

V1.8 adds explicit topology and read-mostly federation. It does not add hosted sync, daemon processes, a global merged graph, external SaaS integrations, arbitrary plugin execution, or generic cross-vault graph mutation.

The only cross-vault write in V1.8 is mutation of the local global registry control plane for topology relationships. Graph writes still happen in exactly one project-local vault at a time.

## Stable Vault Identity

Treat `VaultEntry.id` as the stable `vaultId`. Do not rename the registry field in V1.8 because existing `vault list --json` consumers may already depend on it. CLI topology JSON may expose both `id` and `vaultId` aliases when useful, but the registry stores `id`.

Each project vault should persist its stable identity in `.awg/config.json`:

```json
{
  "vault": {
    "id": "vault:<stable-id>",
    "createdAt": "<iso8601>",
    "identityVersion": 1
  }
}
```

Identity rules:
- If `.awg/config.json` has `vault.id`, registry registration must use that ID.
- If config lacks `vault.id` but the registry has an entry for the canonical path with `id`, backfill that registry ID into config.
- If neither config nor registry can identify the vault, generate a new non-path-derived `vault:<16-hex-or-better>` ID once and persist it before registry write.
- Existing path-derived registry IDs remain valid for old vaults once backfilled. Do not eagerly rewrite them.
- After a project moves, `awg register` should match by config `vault.id` and update the registry path instead of creating a new identity.
- If a project moved before identity was backfilled, AWG cannot prove continuity. Create a new ID and surface a repair suggestion for the old missing registry entry.
- `vault prune` must not silently delete relationships. If a missing vault is pruned, archive or retain affected relationships with diagnostics rather than dropping them without a trace.

## Registry Relationship Storage

Topology relationships are mutable local control-plane state in `~/.awg/registry.json`, not project graph events. Project graph history remains append-only. Unknown registry fields must be preserved on every read/write.

Add a top-level `relationships` array:

```json
{
  "version": "0.1",
  "vaults": [],
  "relationships": [
    {
      "id": "rel:<stable-hash>",
      "fromVaultId": "vault:...",
      "rel": "depends_on",
      "toVaultId": "vault:...",
      "summary": "Portal depends on Sanity schema contracts.",
      "confidence": 1,
      "visibility": "summary",
      "createdAt": "<iso8601>",
      "updatedAt": "<iso8601>",
      "archivedAt": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Relationship ID rules:
- Relationship IDs are deterministic: hash the normalized tuple `{fromVaultId, rel, toVaultId}` after alias normalization.
- Duplicate link commands for the same tuple update summary/confidence/visibility and `updatedAt`; they do not create a second row.
- Archived relationships keep their ID and set `archivedAt`; `vault topology` excludes archived links by default and can include them with an explicit option later if needed.
- Self-links are invalid unless a future version introduces a specific self-reference use case.
- Relationship writes must sort deterministically by active status, fromVaultId, rel, toVaultId, then id.

## Relationship Vocabulary

Canonical stored relationships for V1.8:
- `parent_of`: directional. Inverse display label is `child_of`.
- `depends_on`: directional. Inverse display label is `depended_on_by`.
- `provides_contract_for`: directional. Inverse display label is `consumes_contract_from`.
- `deploys_to`: directional. Inverse display label is `deployed_by`.
- `owns`: directional. Inverse display label is `owned_by`.
- `sibling_of`: symmetric. Normalize from/to ordering for deterministic IDs.
- `related_to`: symmetric fallback. Normalize from/to ordering for deterministic IDs.

Accepted compatibility aliases:
- `child_of` stores the inverse as `parent_of`.
- `consumes_contract_from` stores the inverse as `provides_contract_for`.
- `owned_by` stores the inverse as `owns`.
- `provides_schema_for` normalizes to `provides_contract_for`.
- `consumes_data_from` normalizes to inverse `provides_contract_for`.

Do not store both a relationship and its inverse unless the user explicitly records a different semantic relation. Display can derive inverse labels.

## Visibility

V1.8 visibility values:
- `summary` default: relation, vault metadata, health, and compiled summaries may be surfaced.
- `private`: automatic lenses/handoff may show that a private relation exists but must not import node bodies or rich details from the related vault.
- `full`: allows summary-level compiled surfaces and matched public node summaries, still not wholesale graph dumps.

No V1.8 surface should dump raw related-vault graphs by default.

## Cross-Vault References on Nodes

Do not extend `anchors.kind` for V1.8. Keep anchors for file/symbol/url/command/doc/external references. Store cross-vault references in node fields:

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "crossVaultRefs": [
      {
        "vaultId": "vault:...",
        "nodeId": "n:optional-target-node",
        "rel": "references|affects|requires_update|implements|blocked_by",
        "reason": "Why this node matters to that vault.",
        "status": "open|reviewed|resolved|handoff_recorded",
        "updatedAt": "<iso8601>"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Validation should be conservative:
- Invalid shape is a doctor warning, not a fatal graph error.
- Unknown `rel` values warn with suggestions.
- Missing target vault warns if the vault is not registered.
- Missing `nodeId` is allowed when the related vault target is not known yet.

## Cross-Vault Handoff Convention

Because V1.8 must avoid implicit cross-vault writes, an agent that changes local knowledge with related-vault impact has two options:
- `cd` into the target project, start a run there, and update that vault explicitly.
- Record a local cross-vault handoff item.

A cross-vault handoff item is a task node in the current vault:

```json
{
  "type": "task",
  "title": "Cross-vault handoff: <target vault name>",
  "status": "active",
  "fields": {
    "kind": "cross_vault_handoff",
    "targetVaultId": "vault:...",
    "sourceRunId": "run:...",
    "sourceNodeIds": ["n:..."],
    "reason": "What needs to be updated or reviewed in the related vault."
  }
}
```

Preflight treats this as handling the local obligation when it targets the same vault as an open `crossVaultRefs` item and was created or updated in the current run.

# V1.8 CLI and JSON Contract

This node defines the concrete command behavior expected for V1.8 topology. Existing `awg vault list`, `awg vault info`, and `awg vault prune` behavior must remain compatible.

## New Commands

`awg vault link --to <vault> --rel <rel> [--from <vault|current>] [--summary <text>] [--confidence <0..1>] [--visibility summary|private|full] [--json]`

Creates or updates a registry relationship. `--from` defaults to `current`. Relationship aliases normalize before storage. Duplicate active relationships update in place and return `created: false`.

`awg vault unlink --relationship <relationship-id> [--json]`

Archives a relationship by setting `archivedAt`. This is non-destructive. A tuple form may be added if small and unambiguous, but the relationship ID path is the required V1.8 behavior.

`awg vault topology [--depth <n>] [--json]`

Shows the current vault, direct related vaults, relationship health, stale/missing diagnostics, and why each related vault is surfaced. Default depth is 1. Depth above 1 must be explicit and bounded.

## Selector Resolution

Vault selectors resolve in this order:
1. `current` means the project-local vault found from cwd.
2. Exact vault ID, e.g. `vault:...`.
3. Exact registered path or project path; both `/repo` and `/repo/.awg` should work.
4. Exact registered name.

Rules:
- Ambiguous names fail with `AWG_VAULT_SELECTOR_AMBIGUOUS` and include candidate IDs/paths.
- Missing selectors fail with `AWG_VAULT_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND`.
- Commands that require the current vault fail with `AWG_VAULT_CURRENT_NOT_FOUND` outside a project vault.
- Symlink or unsafe global-registry paths use the existing fail-closed global path policy.

## `vault link --json` Shape

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "created": true,
  "relationship": {
    "id": "rel:...",
    "fromVaultId": "vault:...",
    "rel": "depends_on",
    "toVaultId": "vault:...",
    "summary": "...",
    "confidence": 1,
    "visibility": "summary",
    "createdAt": "...",
    "updatedAt": "..."
  },
  "fromVault": { "id": "vault:...", "name": "...", "path": "..." },
  "toVault": { "id": "vault:...", "name": "...", "path": "..." },
  "warnings": []
}
```

## `vault topology --json` Shape

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "generatedAt": "<iso8601>",
  "depth": 1,
  "currentVault": {
    "id": "vault:...",
    "vaultId": "vault:...",
    "name": "...",
    "path": "...",
    "scope": "project",
    "health": { "exists": true, "built": true, "fatalErrors": 0, "warnings": 0 }
  },
  "relatedVaults": [
    {
      "id": "vault:...",
      "vaultId": "vault:...",
      "name": "...",
      "path": "...",
      "scope": "project",
      "relationships": ["rel:..."],
      "whySurfaced": ["direct_registry_relationship:depends_on"],
      "health": { "exists": true, "built": true },
      "stale": false,
      "summary": { "source": "compiled_resume", "text": "..." }
    }
  ],
  "relationships": [],
  "diagnostics": []
}
```

## Error Shape

JSON errors should be stable and command-like:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "code": "AWG_VAULT_SELECTOR_AMBIGUOUS",
  "message": "Vault selector matches multiple registered vaults.",
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "vault:...", "name": "...", "path": "..." }
  ]
}
```

## Cross-Vault Mutation Policy

Do not add generic `--vault` graph-write support in V1.8. Commands such as `awg add node`, `awg update node`, `awg add evidence`, and `awg run finish` operate on the current project vault only. To write to another vault, the agent must switch cwd into that project and run AWG there.

# V1.8 Retrieval, Compiler, Preflight, Handoff, and Viewer Contract

## Compiler Output

Materialize `.awg/compiled/indexes/topology.json` for the current vault during `awg build`.

Shape:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "generatedAt": "<iso8601>",
  "currentVault": { "id": "vault:...", "name": "...", "path": "...", "scope": "project" },
  "relationships": [],
  "directNeighbors": [],
  "crossVaultRefs": [],
  "diagnostics": []
}
```

Compiler rules:
- Read the global registry, current vault config, current compiled graph, and already-built direct-neighbor compiled summaries only.
- Never build neighbor vaults implicitly.
- Never read neighbor canonical logs by default.
- If neighbor compiled output is missing or stale, include metadata and diagnostics instead of failing the local build.
- Direct-neighbor traversal is the default. Cycles are diagnostics, not fatal errors.
- Every neighbor entry must include `whySurfaced`.

Neighbor summary source priority:
1. Neighbor `.awg/compiled/lenses/resume.json` compact summary if present.
2. Neighbor `.awg/compiled/views/current.json` compact summary if present.
3. Registry metadata only.

## Relevance Rules for Lens and Handoff

`awg lens task` and `awg handoff` may include related-vault context only when at least one deterministic signal is present:
- The task goal matches a direct neighbor name, tag, relationship summary, or relationship type.
- A matched/touched current-vault node has `fields.crossVaultRefs` targeting that vault.
- The active/current run touched a node with cross-vault refs.
- A direct relationship is contract-bearing: `depends_on`, `provides_contract_for`, `deploys_to`, or `owns`.
- A cross-vault handoff task exists for that vault.

Budget rules:
- Related-vault context should be summary-first and compact.
- Default traversal is depth 1.
- Related-vault context should not consume more than roughly 25 percent of lens/handoff budget unless the user explicitly asks for topology details.
- Do not dump full related graphs or raw node bodies by default.

## Agent Retrieval Gap

V1.8 implementation should make implementation details retrievable without manually reading compiled JSON. Add one of these small agent-facing read improvements:
- Preferred: `awg node show <id> [--json]` that returns full node body, fields, blocks, freshness, anchors, edges, and related run attribution.
- Acceptable fallback: `awg lens task --include-bodies` that includes full bodies for top matched spec/standard/requirement/task nodes within budget.

Until that exists, generated implementation prompts must tell agents to inspect `.awg/compiled/graph.json` by node ID after `awg build` when `search` or `lens task` only surfaces summaries.

## Run Finish Preflight

When a run touches nodes with open `fields.crossVaultRefs`, `awg run finish --status completed` should warn unless one of these is true:
- The ref status is `reviewed`, `resolved`, or `handoff_recorded`.
- A cross-vault handoff task targeting that vault was created or updated in the run.
- The run summary explicitly finishes as `partial`, `blocked`, or `failed`, where warnings are surfaced but not made as hard to ignore.

Suggested warning code:
`AWG_RUN_CROSS_VAULT_IMPACT_UNHANDLED`

Suggested fix:
`cd <target-project> && awg run start --goal "Update related vault context"` or create a cross-vault handoff task in the current vault.

## Doctor Diagnostics and Fix Suggestions

Add conservative, non-mutating suggestions for:
- Missing related vault path: suggest `awg register --name <name>` from the target project or a future `vault repair` command if implemented.
- Ambiguous selector/name: suggest using exact `vault:<id>`.
- Archived/missing relationship target: suggest reviewing `awg vault topology --json`.
- Invalid `crossVaultRefs`: suggest correcting the fields, not deleting nodes.
- Stale neighbor build: suggest running `awg build` in that neighbor project.

## Handoff Output

`awg handoff` should include a compact topology section when relevant:
- current vault identity and status
- direct related vaults with relationship labels
- why each vault was surfaced
- cross-vault refs touched by current/recent run
- open cross-vault handoff tasks
- recommended next actions

`awg handoff --json` should include the same data under a stable `topology` object.

## Viewer

If low-risk, add a read-only topology route. It should show current vault, direct neighbors, relationship labels, health/stale/missing status, and links to neighbor viewer files only when available. Missing neighbor compiled data must not crash the viewer.

# V1.8 Test Plan: Cross-Project Topology and Federation

This is the required test inventory for an implementation agent. Tests must isolate HOME/global registry state and temp project roots. Never touch real `~/.awg`.

## Identity and Registry Migration

- Older registry without `relationships` loads and writes back without losing unknown fields.
- Existing registry vault entry with path-derived `id` is backfilled into `.awg/config.json` as `vault.id`.
- New vault registration creates a non-path-derived stable ID and persists it.
- Moving a vault path after identity exists updates the registry path without changing ID.
- Missing vault entries preserve their IDs and relationships.
- `vault prune --yes` does not silently drop relationships; affected links are retained or archived with diagnostics.

## Relationship CLI

- `vault link --from current --to <id> --rel depends_on --json` creates a deterministic relationship.
- Repeating the same link updates summary/confidence/visibility and returns `created:false`.
- Relationship aliases normalize correctly: `child_of`, `owned_by`, `provides_schema_for`, `consumes_data_from`.
- Symmetric relationships normalize ordering for deterministic IDs.
- Unknown relationships, self-links, unknown selectors, and ambiguous names fail with stable JSON error codes.
- `vault unlink --relationship <id>` archives without deleting unrelated registry data.
- Relationship writes preserve unknown top-level registry fields and unknown vault entry fields.

## Topology Compiler and JSON

- `awg build` writes `.awg/compiled/indexes/topology.json` for the current vault.
- Missing neighbor compiled output produces diagnostics but does not fail local build.
- Missing/corrupt/symlinked related vaults produce safe diagnostics.
- Cyclic topology compiles with bounded traversal and warnings, not recursion.
- Direct neighbors are included by default; depth above 1 requires explicit command option.
- Output is deterministic across repeated builds.

## Retrieval, Handoff, and Budgeting

- `awg lens task` includes related vaults when the goal matches direct neighbor metadata.
- `awg lens task` includes related vaults when matched/touched nodes have `fields.crossVaultRefs`.
- `awg lens task` excludes unrelated registered vault bulk.
- Budgeted lens/handoff output does not dump full related graphs.
- Every surfaced related vault includes `whySurfaced`.
- `awg handoff --json` includes topology context under a stable object.
- `awg handoff --no-record` remains non-mutating and should be recommended for read-only reviewers.

## Preflight and Doctor

- `run finish --status completed` warns when touched nodes have open cross-vault refs and no target update or handoff task.
- `--force` finishes while returning/recording unresolved cross-vault warnings.
- Partial/blocked/failed finishes surface warnings but remain usable.
- Doctor fix suggestions for missing/stale/ambiguous related vaults are concrete, conservative, and non-mutating.
- Invalid `crossVaultRefs` warn with suggested field corrections.

## Viewer and Compatibility

- Topology route handles no registry, no relationships, missing neighbor build, and stale neighbor build.
- Node detail can show cross-vault refs without crashing when targets are missing.
- Existing examples still build.
- Older vaults without `vault.id`, topology indexes, or cross-vault refs still compile.
- All existing tests continue passing.

# V1.8 Subagent Review Synthesis

Three independent review agents inspected the V1.8 AWG planning cluster for implementation readiness.

## Consensus

The architecture is correct: explicit topology plus read-mostly federation is the right foundation. The original cluster was discoverable through `awg lens task`, but it was too high-level for a fresh implementation agent to safely build without making product/API decisions.

## Gaps Found

- Vault identity was called stable, but current registry IDs are path-derived and would break when projects move.
- Relationship storage location and JSON shape were not final enough.
- Relationship vocabulary drifted between `provides_schema_for`, `consumes_data_from`, `provides_contract_for`, `consumes_contract_from`, `owns`, and `owned_by`.
- Cross-vault refs had no concrete node field shape.
- Cross-vault handoff/update obligations had no deterministic representation.
- CLI selector rules, JSON outputs, error codes, duplicate behavior, and unlink/archive behavior were not specified.
- Federation output and relevance rules were too vague to test.
- Privacy/visibility behavior needed a conservative V1 contract.
- The current task lens surfaces node summaries but not enough body detail for implementation, so V1.8 should add or document a node-detail retrieval path.
- Test coverage needed explicit failure-mode cases.

## Resulting Action

The review findings were incorporated into implementation-grade AWG spec nodes covering topology contracts, CLI/JSON behavior, retrieval/preflight/handoff behavior, and tests. These nodes should be treated as required implementation inputs before coding V1.8.

Problem:
AWG has project-local vaults and a global registry, but real work often spans multiple repos or nested operating scopes. The client portal, Astro template, and Sanity schema are separate projects with separate AWG vaults, yet agents need to understand that changes in one can require coordinated updates in the others. Business brains may also have top-level operating knowledge with client-specific child vaults underneath.

Goal:
Introduce a local-first project topology layer that lets AWG describe relationships between vaults and expose cross-vault context to CLI, agent instructions, handoff, task lens, and viewer surfaces. The model should support parent/child, sibling, dependency, shared-source, deployment, owns, consumes, and related-project relationships without forcing one global merged graph.

Example shapes:
1. rd-client-portal depends on sanity-master-template for schema/content contracts and astro-master-template for rendered site behavior.
2. astro-master-template consumes Sanity data and may be deployed/controlled through client portal workflows.
3. Reavis Digital may have a business-level AWG vault for SOPs, pricing, services, ads, SEO, contacts, and operating rules, while client-specific AWG vaults can inherit or reference that business context without polluting the core business brain.

Requirements to explore:
- Registry entries need relationship metadata, not only switcher data.
- Nodes need optional project/vault anchors for cross-project relevance.
- Task lens and handoff should surface related vaults and the minimum necessary cross-vault context.
- Viewer should show a top-level project topology and allow drilling into related vaults.
- Agents need clear rules for when to update local knowledge, when to update a related vault, and when to leave a cross-project handoff.
- The design must stay local-first, deterministic, append-only where possible, and avoid daemon/server/sync creep.

Open design question:
The main unresolved choice is whether relationship metadata belongs primarily in ~/.awg/registry.json, in per-vault AWG nodes, or as a compiled overlay derived from both. The likely answer is a small registry topology plus per-vault durable nodes for richer semantics.

Finalized implementation direction after subagent review:
The open design question is resolved for V1.8. Lightweight relationship metadata lives in the global registry top-level relationships array. Rich project-local meaning stays in each project vault as normal AWG nodes, with cross-vault references represented in node fields.crossVaultRefs. The compiler produces a read-mostly topology index for the current vault and reads only already-built direct-neighbor summaries by default.

The canonical stored topology relationships are parent_of, depends_on, provides_contract_for, deploys_to, owns, sibling_of, and related_to. Compatibility aliases such as child_of, owned_by, provides_schema_for, consumes_data_from, and consumes_contract_from must normalize before storage.

Implementation-grade details are now split across these spec nodes:
- n:v1-8-implementation-contract-topology-identity-a-14d2a947 for identity, registry schema, relationship semantics, visibility, cross-vault refs, and handoff item shape.
- n:v1-8-implementation-contract-topology-cli-and-js-342e053b for vault link/unlink/topology command behavior, selector rules, JSON shapes, and error codes.
- n:v1-8-implementation-contract-federation-retrieva-248cf001 for compiler topology index, relevance rules, preflight, doctor, handoff, and viewer behavior.
- n:v1-8-test-plan-cross-project-topology-and-federa-724c41df for concrete test coverage.
- n:v1-8-subagent-review-synthesis-fd654576 for subagent review synthesis.

Purpose:
The cross-vault contract should let AWG represent project families without collapsing them into one storage system. It must support multi-repo products, parent business brains with child client brains, and research/program brains with related execution projects.

Minimum contract:
- Each registered vault has a stable vault id, display name, path, scope, optional domain tags, and last_seen/build metadata.
- Registry topology stores lightweight relationships between vault ids. Relationship records should include fromVaultId, rel, toVaultId, optional summary, optional confidence, created_at, and updated_at.
- Relationship vocabulary should start small: parent_of, child_of, sibling_of, depends_on, provides_contract_for, consumes_contract_from, deploys_to, owns, related_to.
- Per-vault nodes can carry anchors or fields that reference a related vault and optional related node id.
- Compiled topology should resolve registered paths, missing vaults, relationship direction, cycles, stale builds, and related-vault summaries.
- Lenses should expose related-vault context only when relevant to the current goal, touched nodes, anchors, or topology edges.

Agent contract:
- Read related-vault summaries automatically when topology says they may matter.
- Before adding cross-project knowledge, decide whether it belongs in the current vault, a related vault, or a cross-vault handoff.
- Never silently mutate a related vault without an explicit command context and run attribution.
- If a change likely affects a related vault but the agent does not update it, record a cross-vault handoff item.

Human surface contract:
- Viewer overview may show current vault plus directly related vaults.
- A dedicated topology view should show project families and relationship health.
- Node detail should show cross-vault refs and affected related vaults without dumping the other vault contents.

Scale rule:
Only direct neighbors are loaded by default. Broader traversal requires explicit depth or budget options.

Implementation-grade additions after review:
- Treat registry VaultEntry.id as the stable vaultId and persist it in each project vault config under vault.id.
- Add registry.relationships[] as the V1.8 topology storage location; preserve unknown top-level registry fields and unknown vault entry fields.
- Use deterministic relationship IDs from normalized fromVaultId, rel, and toVaultId tuples.
- Do not extend anchor kinds for V1.8; store cross-vault node references in fields.crossVaultRefs.
- Use summary/private/full relationship visibility with summary as the default.
- For V1.8, reject generic cross-vault graph writes. Agents must switch cwd into the target vault to mutate it, or record a local cross-vault handoff task.
- Direct-neighbor traversal remains the default; every surfaced related vault must include whySurfaced.

The detailed contracts are n:v1-8-implementation-contract-topology-identity-a-14d2a947, n:v1-8-implementation-contract-topology-cli-and-js-342e053b, and n:v1-8-implementation-contract-federation-retrieva-248cf001.

body:
Risks and mitigations:

1. Scope confusion
Agents may write client-specific facts into the business vault or global/product facts into a client vault. Mitigate with explicit vault ownership, visible target-vault prompts, run attribution, and handoff warnings when a related vault is affected but not updated.

2. Context explosion
A related-vault graph can become huge. Mitigate with direct-neighbor default traversal, hard budgets, summaries first, opt-in depth, and goal-matched retrieval only.

3. Stale cross-vault links
Related vaults may move, be deleted, or have stale compiled output. Mitigate with stable vault ids, path repair suggestions, last_seen/build metadata, and doctor warnings for missing/stale vaults.

4. Folder hierarchy false positives
Nested directories do not always mean parent-child knowledge ownership. Mitigate by treating folder layout as discovery evidence only; semantic relationships must be explicit.

5. Accidental cross-vault mutation
A command intended for the current project could modify a related vault. Mitigate by making cross-vault writes require explicit target-vault flags, confirmation in human CLI output, and run attribution in the target vault.

6. Security and privacy leakage
A high-level business vault could surface client-sensitive data, or a client vault could expose unrelated business data. Mitigate with no automatic global merging, summary-only default surfaces, sensitive diagnostics, and optional relationship visibility fields.

7. Cycles and ambiguous ownership
Project families can have cycles like portal <-> Astro <-> Sanity. Mitigate with relationship types, directionality, cycle diagnostics as warnings not fatal errors, and ownership-specific rels such as owns/provides_contract_for/consumes_contract_from.

8. Registry corruption or portability issues
The registry is a control plane and can drift from reality. Mitigate with schema validation, backups via append-like update events where practical, repair suggestions, and keeping canonical project knowledge inside project vaults.

9. Agents ignoring topology
The feature fails if agents do not check it. Mitigate by adding topology checks to handoff, lens task, generated AGENTS.md, and finish preflight when related-vault impacts exist.

10. Over-modeling too early
A large ontology could make AWG harder to use. Mitigate with a tiny relationship vocabulary, extension fields, and measured evolution from real dogfood cases.

Additional risks identified by subagent review:

11. Path-derived vault ID breakage
Existing registry IDs are path-derived, so moved projects can break topology links. Mitigate by persisting vault.id in project config and matching future registrations by that ID.

12. Registry lost updates or unknown-field loss
The registry is a mutable control-plane file. Mitigate with stable stringify, atomic-ish writes consistent with existing registry behavior, deterministic sorting, and preservation of unknown top-level/vault/relationship fields.

13. Cross-vault reference ambiguity
If refs are hidden in free text, preflight cannot reason about them. Mitigate with fields.crossVaultRefs and conservative doctor warnings for malformed refs.

14. Over-broad related-vault context
A topology feature can become a context dump. Mitigate with summary-first surfaces, direct-neighbor defaults, whySurfaced explanations, and budget caps.

15. Lens omission risk
If implementation details are stored only in long node bodies but lenses show only summaries, agents may miss requirements. Mitigate with a node-detail read command or lens body inclusion for top matched spec nodes.

title: V1.8 risk register: cross-project brains

body:
Decision:
V1.8 should introduce explicit cross-project topology. The global registry should remain a local control plane, but it should be able to store stable vault ids and lightweight relationships between registered vaults. Each vault remains canonical for its own durable knowledge. The compiler can derive a read-mostly federation overlay for task lens, handoff, doctor, and viewer surfaces.

Why this is the best foundation:
- It preserves project-local ownership and append-only vault history.
- It lets related projects be discovered without dumping every graph into context.
- It works for sibling repos, parent/child business-client structures, and dependency chains.
- It gives agents enough map context to know where related knowledge lives while keeping writes explicit.
- It avoids daemon, sync, database, server, and multi-user complexity.

Rejected alternatives:
1. One global merged graph: simpler to query, but ownership becomes unclear, context grows fast, and privacy/scope boundaries become fragile.
2. Folder hierarchy inference only: convenient, but too ambiguous; folder layout is not a reliable semantic relationship.
3. Automatic cross-vault writes: powerful but dangerous; agents could silently mutate the wrong business/client/project brain.
4. External sync or hosted coordination: too heavy for the local-first product and outside the current scope.

Final direction:
Start with explicit links, read-only traversal, deterministic indexes, and agent-facing prompts that require deliberate local-vault updates or cross-vault handoff notes when a related vault should be changed.

Clarification after review:
For V1.8, explicit write policy means no generic cross-vault graph mutation flag on add/update/evidence/run commands. Topology commands may mutate the global registry relationship control plane. Durable graph writes remain scoped to the current project-local vault. To update a related vault, an agent must switch cwd into that project and run AWG there, or leave a structured cross-vault handoff task in the current vault.
